lines.text: Can a single catastrophic volcanic eruption actually plunge the entire planet into an icy volcanic winter?
History has proven that the answer is an undeniable yes.
When Indonesia's Mount Tambora erupted in eighteen fifteen, it blasted sixty million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere.
The sulfur reacted with water vapor to form a shimmering global blanket of sulfate aerosol droplets.
This volcanic veil reflected incoming sunlight back into space, cooling global temperatures for three straight years.
Eighteen sixteen became known as the 'Year Without a Summer', with blizzards hitting New England in July.
Massive volcanic eruptions hold the raw power to rewrite global climate overnight.
